relations.note: Taú fathers Moñái through his forced union with Keraná.
Keraná bears Moñái third among seven monstrous children.
Arasy's curse causes Keraná's pregnancies to produce seven monsters, including Moñái.
Teju Jagua is one of Moñái's six monstrous brothers.

relations.myth: Wedding gathering in the burning cave
relations.note: Moñái summons Teju Jagua to the false wedding where both are trapped.
Mbói Tu’ĩ is one of Moñái's six monstrous brothers.

relations.myth: Wedding gathering in the burning cave
relations.note: Moñái summons Mbói Tu’ĩ to the false wedding where both are trapped.
Jasy Jatere is one of Moñái's six monstrous brothers.

relations.myth: Wedding gathering in the burning cave
relations.note: Moñái summons Jasy Jatere to the false wedding where both are trapped.
Kurupí is one of Moñái's six monstrous brothers.
Moñái's robberies and Kurupí's sexual violence jointly afflict Atyrá.

relations.myth: Wedding gathering in the burning cave
relations.note: Kurupí joins Moñái and their brothers at Porãsy's fatal false wedding.
Ao-Ao is one of Moñái's six monstrous brothers.

relations.myth: Wedding gathering in the burning cave
relations.note: Moñái summons Ao-Ao to the false wedding where both are trapped.
Huisõ is one of Moñái's six monstrous brothers.

relations.myth: Wedding gathering in the burning cave
relations.note: Moñái summons Huisõ to the false wedding where both are trapped.
Porãsy professes love and offers marriage to lure the aged Moñái.
Porãsy deceives Moñái into assembling all his brothers inside a cave.

relations.myth: Porãsy's sacrifice and the burning cave
relations.note: Porãsy orders the sealed cave burned, killing Moñái, his brothers, and herself.

relations.myth: Plan to destroy the seven monsters
relations.note: Tume-Arandu strategically opposes Moñái by directing the plan undertaken by Porãsy.
Cadogan says the monkey-monster Ka’i jagua lives associated with Moñái.
Cadogan's ambiguous wording may present Ta’ytetu Jagua as another designation for Moñái.
Alternatively, Cadogan's wording may make Ta’ytetu Jagua another monster associated with Ka’i jagua and Moñái.
